headline: Benchmark design determines which structure and affinity prediction gains hold up
label: Biomolecular Prediction Benchmarks
summary: Fresh preprints test co-folding, TCR-pMHC modeling, and water placement on curated or held-out sets rather than relying on headline architecture gains.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation design: predictive gains are assessed under curated or held-out protocols that expose where models fail. HuMonoAg-Bench benchmarks ten co-folding protocols on 412 antibody-antigen complexes, with recent methods reaching DockQ ≥0.49 for about half of post-cutoff Fv. Thal-Kak unifies five all-atom structure predictors and finds that model mixing improves oracle sampling while selection lags, a sampling-selection gap. For TCR-pMHC specificity, AlphaFold3-based structural modeling combined with cluster-based label denoising improves prediction for unseen peptides, outperforming AF2.3. InterPET curates a 937-training, 139-test PETase benchmark comparing ESM-2, ProtT5, and AAC/CTD embeddings. CIR-DDG adds 22 cross-chain geometry descriptors as a residual adapter on fixed backbones for antibody-antigen ddG on SKEMPI. WaterFlow predicts ordered water positions, and the OpenMM ML/MM-MMGBSA workflow is benchmarked on 199 complexes.
